title: SCIPE: A Non-Compensatory Diagnostic Framework for Sub-National SDG-Aligned Quality of Life Assessment
content: Measuring multidimensional Quality of Life (QoL) increasingly relies on composite indicators to guide sustainable development policy. However, standard linear aggregation frameworks generally assume full compensability, allowing strong performance in one domain to mathematically mask severe deficits in another. For policymakers, this compensatory masking may conceal structural imbalances across sectors, obscuring localized vulnerabilities critical for targeted interventions. To address this diagnostic gap, we introduce the Sustainable Composite Indicator for Policy Evidence (SCIPE), a granular QoL assessment framework that explicitly penalizes horizontal imbalances across SDG-aligned dimensions. Using Bangladesh’s 64 administrative districts as a representative case study, we construct a multi-domain baseline that integrates traditional socio-economic metrics with satellite-derived night-time light data. SCIPE employs Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for data-driven indicator weighting and the Mazziotta-Pareto Index (MPI) to enforce an explicit variance penalty. Sensitivity analysis against the Human Development Index (HDI) confirms convergent validity while demonstrating SCIPE’s sensitivity to inter-sectoral volatility. Empirical findings reveal that penalizing horizontal variance significantly reconfigures district rankings: rewarding balanced developmental trajectories while exposing hidden trade-offs, such as ecological and public health deficits within affluent industrial corridors. Ultimately, this study demonstrates that aggregation choices fundamentally dictate policy interpretation, underscoring the necessity of evaluating balanced progress rather than relying solely on macro-level averages.
